$comment: Where `derm connect <agent> --gate` registers derm's gate, one object per agent (wave 4 lane Q, T2.8). Transcribed from the packages that own each gate: lane L's packages/derm-hooks-claude-compat/src/registration.ts (branch wip/L-hooks-claude at 12d2c86), lane N's packages/derm-hooks-native/registration/<agent>/ and its README table (lane/N-hooks-native at 85592cf), and docs/install/agents.md (main at 824ae83) for the agents whose gate installs through their own command. Lane Q keeps this table in its own folder so lanes L, N and P never share a file with it; integration w4 may move each object into its agent's preset row. Placeholders: {command} is the agent's `command` with {node} and {hook_file} filled; {hook_dir} is the package folder given with --hook; {hook_url} is file:// plus that folder; {version} is derm's own version. A string is a placeholder only when it is the whole value, except in `command` and `commands`. `marker` finds derm's own entry, so a second --gate replaces it and never adds a second gate. Step kinds: json-array-entry, json-member, toml-array-entry, toml-set, owned-file, plugin-folder, json-permission (OpenCode's and Kilo's `permission` keys, set only where that narrows), commands (print only). `mergeChain` lists the global files an agent deep-merges, in its order: derm writes the last one that exists (else `path`) and reads the others first. Wave 5b lane 5bF: a command-hook row's `command` is `{derm} hook <agent> <event>`, {derm} being this derm's own real path, a plain path to a file only you or root can write in a folder of the same kind, so no --hook folder and no node (contracts/hook-dialects.md 9.1; rules case 227). `markers` lists what finds derm's own entry: the first is in what derm writes now, the rest in what an older derm wrote, so a second --gate replaces a wave 4 node entry. Step kind text-file writes one file of plain text derm owns alone (Hermes's derm-path), only into a folder that already exists when `folderMustExist`.

agents.name: Codex
agents.command: & '{derm}' hook codex pre; if ($null -eq $LASTEXITCODE) { [Console]::Error.WriteLine('derm: derm.exe did not start'); exit 2 }; exit $LASTEXITCODE
agents.commandPost: & '{derm}' hook codex post; if ($null -eq $LASTEXITCODE) { [Console]::Error.WriteLine('derm: derm.exe did not start'); exit 1 }; exit $LASTEXITCODE
agents.source: fix pass 8 (the Windows box, 15 Nov 2026): Codex 0.167.2 reads the user's $CODEX_HOME/hooks.json (codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/discovery.rs:176-180, config/src/state.rs:239-243) and runs a hook's line through the session's shell, which on Windows is PowerShell (shell-command/src/shell_detect.rs:363-365: pwsh, else powershell), as `<shell> -NoProfile -Command <line>` (core/src/session/mod.rs:5805-5813, hooks/src/engine/command_runner.rs:444-470); cmd.exe /C only when the session has no shell. So derm.exe is called by its absolute path with PowerShell's call operator, in single quotes, and `exit $LASTEXITCODE` gives Codex derm's exit code, which -Command would turn into 1 (a non-blocking error) (V by run on the box: exit 2 blocks and the program gets the hook's stdin). When derm.exe does not start (moved, removed, blocked), `&` is a statement error and $LASTEXITCODE is $null, which `exit` turns into 0, an allow; so that case writes a reason and exits 2 (fix pass 8's review, run on the box). Fix pass 7's cmd.exe line ran in PowerShell as a parse error, which Codex lets through. cmd.exe runs the line instead when the session has no shell or not exactly one local environment (environment_selection.rs:1466-1477), where the leading `&` fails and the call goes through: a known gap.
notes: Then trust both hooks in /hooks: Codex skips an untrusted hook without a word (case 70), and asks again when a hook changes.
Codex lets a call through when its hook process dies or times out (case 70); derm's hook never crashes on purpose and caps its own waits below this timeout.
derm.exe's path may not hold a single quote (or a curly one), which would end PowerShell's quoted path.

agents.source: fix pass 9 (Tony's go of 15 Nov 2026, note BG section 1): Cursor runs a hook on Windows through PowerShell and pipes the JSON into it (cursor.com/docs/hooks: "On Windows, the desktop app runs hook commands through PowerShell and pipes the JSON into the command"); that sentence is about the desktop app; cursor-agent, the CLI this row is for, composes `$OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Content -LiteralPath <payload> -Raw | & { $input | <command> }` (read from the installed agent CLI 2026.09.28, RepoQL/RepoQL#17; logged in forum.cursor.com/t/168129 and t/170945). Run on the box under that exact wrapper with Windows PowerShell 5.1 (fix pass 9): stdin starts with a BOM (efbbbf), derm allows and denies, and exit 2 comes out of the script block. So derm.exe is called as on Codex's Windows row: by its absolute path in single quotes with the call operator, a reason and exit 2 when it does not start, else derm's exit code. failClosed: a crash, timeout, non-zero exit or no output blocks (cursor.com/docs/hooks). Not run against a real Cursor (it needs an account, call 8).
notes: Not run against the real CLI (it needs an account, call 8).

With Git Bash's MSYSTEM set, cursor-agent runs a PowerShell-built hook line with bash, so every hook fails and, failing closed, every call is blocked (Cursor staff reproduced it 12 Aug 2026; forum.cursor.com/t/168129). Start Cursor from an environment without MSYSTEM.
derm.exe's path may not hold a single quote (or a curly one), which would end PowerShell's quoted path.
